name: Yellow bell pepper (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Yellow bell pepper (Capsicum annuum) [Vegetables] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: DTU, DUKE, Edible Medicinal And Non-Medicinal Plants: Volume 6, Fruits. By T. K. Lim, MANUAL, PHENOL EXPLORER, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA FoodData Central FDC 169383 (Peppers, sweet, yellow, raw)
USDA FoodData Central FDC 170427 (Peppers, sweet, green, raw) – analog for Se, choline, vitamin K
Ciqual / Aprifel yellow pepper nutritional sheet
nutritionvalue.org (USDA-derived) – yellow sweet pepper amino-acid profile
Wahyuni et al., comprehensive Capsicum annuum fruit-quality / organic-acid study (PMC9871545)
Antonio et al. 2009, Variability for free sugars and organic acids in Capsicum chinense (PMID 19235156)
provenance.curation_notes: Dominant carbon/energy sources: free hexoses fructose (~2.3 g) + glucose (~2.0 g), with essentially no sucrose in this ripe (yellow) fruit; the leading organic-acid carbon source is citric acid (~0.4 g/100g, rises with ripening) followed by malic (~0.12 g, falls with ripening), fumaric, alpha-ketoglutarate and oxalic. Yellow bell pepper is exceptionally vitamin-C-rich (~120–184 mg/100g). Removed 24 FooDB noise entries (heavy metals, non-nutritive trace elements, and implausible animal/synthetic
curation_added: citric acid (dominant organic acid, was absent)
quantified vitamins and minerals (K, P, Mg, Ca, Fe, Zn, etc.)

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
